editorial.headline: Rubber and Resin Cultivation With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers rubber and other sap-producing crops from planting to post-harvest, with foreign ownership nationally open and no Bali PMA block recorded.
editorial.body:
This activity is agricultural before it is industrial: the field work of growing rubber trees and other plants that produce sap or resin, including damar, pine, and kemenyan. Its scope is broad enough to follow the crop through the practical life of cultivation, from land preparation and planting to maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest work when those steps are carried out as one continuous activity.

It also reaches into two important edges of the sector. First, it includes rubber and other sap-producing crop activity conducted inside forest areas. Second, it covers planting these crops to produce seed in the form of grains or seeds. In plain English, this is not merely a plantation label for mature rubber output; it can also describe the agricultural base that prepares, grows, maintains, harvests, and supports seed production for rubber and comparable sap-producing plants.

The registration audience is wide. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so it is not reserved only for large plantation groups. A small agricultural operator, a mid-sized grower, or a larger structured business can all sit within the same activity description if the actual work matches the scope: cultivation of rubber or other sap-producing crops, including the connected land, planting, maintenance, harvest, post-harvest, forest-area, or seed-production activities described in the record.

The national foreign-investment position is straightforward. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. The Bali picture is equally important, and in this case it does not reverse the national answer. Bali's moratorium blocks PMA registration for Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities across the province, but this record is not blocked: the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. For a foreign-owned setup, the honest reading is therefore clean: nationally open, up to full foreign ownership, and not recorded as blocked by the Bali PMA moratorium.
